raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I am 76 now, my back is not what it was, but I know this soil. I do not need books to tell me what to plant.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize. That is what I have always done. That is what my father did. The land here is flat and the soil is good for it. After the wheat comes off in June, the maize goes straight in — the rains come in summer and the maize does not need as much watering. Then in October I plant wheat again. This rotation, I have done it fifty times.

I keep about 5 mu of cropland now. My son helps sometimes but he works in the city. I hire a machine for plowing and harvesting — I cannot do that myself anymore at my age.

For seed, I buy the improved wheat seed from the village supply store. I have tried the old varieties but the yields are lower. For maize I use the hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, I have used it for many years, it is reliable. I know some younger farmers use newer varieties but I trust what I know.

Fertilizer: I put more rather than less. My grandfather said a hungry crop gives nothing back. I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress the wheat at jointing. Water is the real worry — we have to pump from underground. I irrigate wheat four times: before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. Maize, the summer rains help, I only need to irrigate once or twice if it is dry.

I spray for aphids and rust on the wheat — two or three times depending on how bad it looks. Maize I spray once for fall armyworm, it has gotten worse these past years.
